papers.title: [Editorial] Getting ready for the next pandemic
papers.summary: The tragic death, disability, and chaos wrought by the COVID-19 are fading from collective memory. The pandemic created a global health crisis that led to more than 7 million reported deaths, an estimated 28 million excess deaths, and profound health, economic, and social disruption. It exposed critical failures in pandemic preparedness and weaknesses in social and health systems. Yet even though the risk of pandemics is growing, the world has failed to be ready for the next one. On Sept 21, a new Lancet Commission report is published, The National University of Singapore (NUS)–Lancet Pandemic Readiness through Institutions, Mobilising Communities, and Equity (PRIME) Commission.

papers.title: [Comment] Beyond rescue: building a resilient health system after Nepal's 2026 flood
papers.summary: Nepal's government health system operates on local as well as provincial and federal government levels, with local facilities focusing on basic health services, while provincial and federal hospitals provide specialised services.1 Nepal has endorsed universal health coverage; however, resource limitation, an ineffective health insurance system, and geographical inaccessibility in rural areas have hindered government capacity to provide basic and specialised health services to all people. The universal health coverage effective coverage index was only 47·3% in 2019.

papers.title: [Comment] Cardiac resynchronisation therapy: 30 years of progress
papers.summary: Cardiac resynchronisation therapy with biventricular pacing (BiV-CRT) revolutionised the treatment of heart failure in patients with left bundle-branch block (LBBB). Its development, founded upon observations that LBBB leads to cardiac impairment,1 progressed to finding that combining a lead implanted on the left ventricular free wall with a lead in the right ventricle could provide drastic improvements in acute cardiac function in patients with LBBB.2 The development of dedicated leads facilitated the fully transvenous approach to BiV-CRT, with the left ventricular free wall targeted by using a ventricular branch of the coronary sinus.

papers.title: [Comment] Acute heart failure in Africa: new causes, unchanged outcomes
papers.summary: More than 15 years ago, the original Sub-Saharan Africa Survey of Heart Failure (THESUS-HF) provided one of the first prospective, multinational descriptions of acute heart failure in sub-Saharan Africa.1 THESUS-HF found that patients with acute heart failure in sub-Saharan Africa were young, with near-equal incidence in men and women, that incidence was driven overwhelmingly by non-ischaemic disease, especially hypertensive and rheumatic heart diseases, and that short-term prognosis was poor.1 The study reframed heart failure in Africa as a distinct clinical entity rather than a footnote to high-income cohorts.

papers.title: [Comment] Late-onset seizures as a sentinel of Alzheimer's disease progression in Down syndrome
papers.summary: Epilepsy is a common co-occurring condition in older adults with Down syndrome and frequently associated with the emergence of Alzheimer's disease-related cognitive decline.1 Likely to be under-recognised and often untreated in the earlier stages, late-onset myoclonic epilepsy in Down syndrome (LOMEDS) presents as myoclonic or tonic–clonic seizures and can be both a manifestation of underlying Alzheimer's disease pathology and an accelerator of disease progression.2 How seizure onset timing in adults with Down syndrome relates to Alzheimer's disease symptoms and progression remains unclear, complicating interpretation of decline and clinical management.

papers.title: [Comment] The Accra Reset must turn sovereignty into country power
papers.summary: Global health is experiencing severe disruption in its traditional governance architecture, precipitated by drastic changes in financial flows, which has greatly affected low-income and middle-income countries. These countries are asked to coordinate external inputs from global health institutions while having little control over their mandates, boards, funding, or incentives. Ministries of health remain accountable for health outcomes while external partners retain authority over priorities, financing channels, indicators, and data.

papers.title: [Comment] Offline: Bringing hope, organising action
papers.summary: What happened to the radicalism that once motivated those struggling on the front lines of global health? The values embodied in global health were a credo for living, a kind of personal faith. But look at us now. We are stumbling in a foggy stupor, unable to plan, unwilling to campaign, unready to lead. Signs of defeat were visible long ago. The sharp focus on a few objectives during the Millennium Development Goal era, which inspired so many, evolved into a comforting blancmange of hopelessly unrealistic aspirations—otherwise called the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)—designed more to appease development cognoscenti than to solve the challenges of those they claimed to serve.

papers.title: [World Report] Front-line medicine on the Thailand–Myanmar border
papers.summary: The Mae Tao Clinic is providing essential medical care to many who have fled Myanmar. Sima Barmania reports from the Thailand–Myanmar border.

papers.title: [World Report] Platform trials: the study design transforming infectious diseases
papers.summary: Fast, flexible, and able to enrol large numbers of participants, adaptive platform trials are helping to address long-standing clinical questions and the latest emerging infections. Talha Burki reports.

papers.title: [Perspectives] Teresa Lambe: making vaccines, saving lives
papers.summary: Teresa Lambe, the Calleva Head of Vaccine Immunology and Professor of Vaccinology and Immunology at the University of Oxford, UK, is one of those academics who wears many different hats. She describes herself in different ways depending on to whom she is speaking: “either a manufacturer, an immunologist, or a vaccinologist. But really, I am an immunologist who makes vaccines and tries to get them all the way through from concept to licensure”. Where is she channelling these various identities and energies at the moment? “Pretty much solely focused on and obsessed with the Bundibugyo Ebola virus outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo”, she says.

papers.title: [Perspectives] Global health in the crosswinds
papers.summary: Over the past two centuries, global health has evolved from being a domain of public health enmeshed in geopolitics to becoming a multidisciplinary platform for the marriage of development with diplomacy. Comparative epidemiological profiling of countries began during the 19th century under the term “geographical pathology”. By the late 19th century, European colonial powers started using the term “tropical medicine” to describe the health challenges that confronted them in colonised countries of Asia and Africa.

papers.title: [Obituary] Lesley Southgate
papers.summary: General practitioner, academic, and an authority on physician competence and performance. Born on Sept 25, 1943, in Luton, UK, she died from pneumonia and Alzheimer's disease in Sunderland, UK, on July 18, 2026, aged 82 years.

papers.title: [Correspondence] Enhancing preparedness for the impending super El Niño
papers.summary: Peak predictions of the emerging El Niño event suggest that it could reach a maximum monthly sea surface temperature anomaly of +3·9°C (median forecast),1 substantially surpassing the highest recorded magnitude of +2·75°C set by the 2015–16 El Niño.2 El Niño is a natural phenomenon, occurring every 2–7 years as part of the El Niño-Southern Oscillation cycle, but it is happening against a background of human-induced climate change, which could result in more extreme global impacts over time.

papers.title: [Correspondence] Gaza: who can afford to lose hope?
papers.summary: In 2018, my colleagues and I wrote in The Lancet that international action was needed to avert further loss of “life, dignity, and hope” among Palestine refugees.1 Since 2018, the humanitarian situation in Gaza has deteriorated dramatically, and the tragedy continues today. Watching it from the outside, I find myself thinking about the importance of the last word in that phrase: hope.

papers.title: [Correspondence] Prison health as longitudinal care: lessons from Brazil
papers.summary: Talha Burki's World Report1 powerfully illustrates that prison health is shaped by complex, overlapping needs: multimorbidity, mental distress, substance use, premature ageing, and fragile access to care. From Brazil—home to the world's third-largest prison population, estimated at 850 000 individuals in 20242—we recognise this landscape and address an aspect that remains underexplored in the World Report: prisons as territories of longitudinal care.

papers.title: [Correspondence] Fabricated citations at scale: from detection to prevention
papers.summary: Maxim Topaz and colleagues1 report accelerating rates of fabricated references in peer-reviewed literature, highlighting a substantial threat to biomedical publishing that is likely resulting from the growing use of large language models (LLMs) by researchers when preparing articles.2 However, the reliability of their estimates depends on the LLM classifier used at a decisive point in their pipeline to conduct their study.

papers.title: [Correspondence] Fabricated citations at scale: from detection to prevention
papers.summary: Maxim Topaz and colleagues1 document an important pattern: fabricated references in the indexed biomedical literature—topically adapted—largely escape post-publication correction. The qualitative finding is robust, however, the reported 12-fold increase between 2023 and early 2026 is not.

papers.title: [Correspondence] Fabricated citations at scale: from detection to prevention – Authors' reply
papers.summary: We thank Tiange Li and colleagues, and Ali Mohamed Mousa and Mervat Mahmoud-Katheer for their comments on our Correspondence.1 Our study was among the first systematic, large-scale audits of fabricated citations in biomedicine. Across 2 471 758 papers and 125·6 million references, we identified 4046 references that could not be found, across 2810 publications, and documented a greater than 12-fold increase in the quarterly rate of detected fabricated references per 10 000 papers.1 Li and colleagues and Mousa and Mahmoud-Katheer question our language model step and interpretation of the observed trend; we address both concerns and consider how publishers should act once fabricated references are identified.

papers.title: [Correspondence] Mechanism–endpoint matching in lupus: WILLOW Cohort B
papers.summary: The Cohort B results of the WILLOW trial separate two questions often conflated in lupus trials: whether a drug altered the disease biology, and whether the chosen composite endpoint was structured to detect that alteration.1 Although enpatoran failed the primary multiple comparison procedure-modelling British Isles Lupus Assessment Group-based Composite Lupus Assessment (BICLA) dose–response analysis (p=0·14) in the study by Eric F Morand and colleagues,1 the non-monotonic response pattern (39% placebo vs 58%, 49%, and 49% across doses) suggests a pharmacodynamic plateau rather than a lack of activity.

papers.title: [Correspondence] Mechanism–endpoint matching in lupus: WILLOW Cohort B – Authors' reply
papers.summary: We thank Huihua Ding and colleagues for their thoughtful comments regarding the Cohort B results of the WILLOW trial in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE).1 In this study, all doses of the Toll-like receptor 7 and 8 (TLR7/8) inhibitor enpatoran were associated with higher attainment of the composite outcome measure—ie, British Isles Lupus Assessment Group-based Composite Lupus Assessment (BICLA)—but the prespecified primary outcome of showing a dose–response with this endpoint was not reached.1

papers.title: [Correspondence] Cardiovascular outcomes in coronary microvascular dysfunction: the Multicenter FLOW-CMD Registry
papers.summary: The FLOW-CMD Registry1 represents one of the largest contemporary assessments of coronary microvascular dysfunction in a broad population undergoing invasive coronary physiological evaluation, including patients with acute coronary syndrome and those requiring percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). The study expands awareness of coronary microvascular dysfunction beyond patients with non-obstructive coronary artery disease.

papers.title: [Correspondence] Cardiovascular outcomes in coronary microvascular dysfunction: the Multicenter FLOW-CMD Registry
papers.summary: In their recent Article,1 Joo Myung Lee and colleagues used bolus thermodilution (coronary flow reserve [CFR] <2·0 and the index of microcirculatory resistance [IMR] ≥25) to define coronary microvascular dysfunction and found it in 163 (16·3%) of 1003 patients. One in five of these cases were in people with obstructive epicardial coronary artery disease, but 10% occurred in those without obstructive epicardial coronary artery disease. In this latter group, prognoses were worse, with adverse events occurring in a quarter (ten of 40) of those with coronary microvascular dysfunction compared with less than a tenth in those without (30 of 390 patients; hazard ratio 3·45 [95% CI 1·69–7·06]; p=0·0003).

papers.title: [Articles] Aetiology, management, and outcomes of acute heart failure in 17 African countries (THESUS-HF II): a prospective, multicentre, observational cohort study
papers.summary: Compared with THESUS-HF, THESUS-HF II suggests an evolving aetiological profile of acute heart failure in Africa, although differences in ascertainment and diagnostic capability might have contributed to the apparent aetiological shift. High mortality in this relatively young cohort highlights the importance of heart failure prevention, access to cardiac care, guideline-directed therapy, and post-discharge follow-up. These findings suggest that short-term acute heart failure outcomes are not driven by its demographic, aetiological, and echocardiographic factors.

papers.title: [Articles] Natural history and clinical impact of epilepsy in adults with Down syndrome: a multicentre clinical study
papers.summary: Epilepsy increases sharply after symptomatic Alzheimer's disease onset in people with Down syndrome. The association of epilepsy with reduced survival and accelerated cognitive decline underscores the need for targeted preventive and therapeutic strategies against Alzheimer's disease-related epileptogenesis and hyperexcitability.

papers.title: [The Lancet Commissions] The NUS–Lancet PRIME Commission: transforming pandemic readiness for equity
papers.summary: The National University of Singapore (NUS)–Lancet Pandemic Readiness through Institutions, Mobilising Communities, and Equity (PRIME) Commission redefines pandemic readiness and offers a practical blueprint for whole-of-society pandemic planning and implementation. Drawing on the hard lessons of the COVID-19 pandemic, the Commission brings together evidence from 20 countries, including interviews with members of diverse communities and groups, future scenarios, and epidemiological modelling. By integrating lived experience with systems analysis and forward-looking evidence, the Commission sets out how governments, institutions, and communities can move from formal plans to people-centred protection across all stages of a health crisis.

papers.title: [Editorial] Counteracting the rise of antimicrobial resistance in Shigella
papers.summary: Shigella, a Gram-negative bacterium, causes shigellosis, characterised by intestinal symptoms. Shigellosis is one of the leading causes of global diarrhoeal disease deaths, especially in children younger than 5 years. Shigella disproportionately affects low-income and middle-income countries (LMICs), where transmission occurs mainly through the oral–faecal route due to poor water, sanitation, and hygiene practices. Shigella is divided into four main species: S dysenteriae, S boydii, S flexneri, and S sonnei, of which all have multiple serotypes except S flexneri.

papers.title: [Comment] South Sudan's first 100 days of Bundibugyo Ebola readiness
papers.summary: When the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DR Congo) and Uganda declared an outbreak of Ebola virus disease caused by Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) on May 15, 2026, South Sudan looked likely to be the next country affected. Modelling estimated a 70% probability that at least one case would cross into the country within 12 weeks,1 driven by intense population movement across porous borders with DR Congo and Uganda. The amplifiers that have propelled the epidemic in the Ituri province—armed conflict, displacement, and a fragile health system—are at least as pronounced in South Sudan, and pathogens do not respect borders.

papers.title: [Correspondence] Cross-reactive Bundibugyo antibody responses in Guinean survivors of Ebola virus and recipients of rVSVΔG-ZEBOV-GP (Ervebo) in an outbreak setting
papers.summary: Control of the ongoing outbreak of Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) in DR Congo, already the largest on record, has been hindered by the absence of licensed vaccines. Although BDBV-specific vaccines are under development, the licensed and stockpiled Ebola virus vaccine (rVSVΔG-ZEBOV-GP; Ervebo, Merck Sharp & Dohme) warrants evaluation as a potential stopgap measure, particularly for those at high exposure risk (eg, front-line responders, health-care workers, and contacts). rVSVΔG-ZEBOV-GP has conferred partial heterologous protection against BDBV challenge in non-human primates,1,2 and mixed BDBV responses have been detected in west African3 and Congolese participants4 receiving this vaccine.

papers.title: [News] Research in brief
papers.summary: A cohort study in France assessed the monoclonal antibody nirsevimab against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in infants at 1 year and 2 years after immunisation. Outcomes were examined in infants born before the first RSVpreF vaccination campaign for pregnant women started in September 2024. Nirsevimab was associated with lower rates of RSV-lower respiratory tract-related hospitalisations during the first year after immunisation: 299 (0·8%) of 37 366 immunised versus 899 (2·4%) of 37 366 non-immunised infants in 2023, and 456 (0·5%) of 87 763 immunised versus 1711 (1.9%) of 87 763 non-immunised infants in 2024 (weighted hazard ratios 0·34, 95% CI 0·30–0·39 for the 2023 cohort and 0·28, 0.25–0·31 for the 2024 cohort, corresponding to nirsevimab effectiveness estimates of 66% and 72%, respectively).

papers.title: [Obituary] Bruce Ribner
papers.summary: Pioneering infectious disease physician and epidemiologist died on July 19, 2026, aged 80 years.

papers.title: [Profile] Mahboubeh Hajiabdolbaghi—advancing ID care in Iran
papers.summary: Mahboubeh Hajiabdolbaghi was born and raised in Tehran, where her parents encouraged education, curiosity, and independence. She studied medicine at Tehran University of Medical Sciences (TUMS), at a time when only around one in ten medical students was female. “The passion for learning my mother and father gave me has stayed with me throughout my life”, she tells The Lancet Infectious Diseases. She retired as Professor of Infectious Diseases at TUMS in 2022 and but continues in clinical practice in Tehran.

papers.title: [Clinical Picture] Lymphoma-like endoscopic appearance of lymphogranuloma venereum
papers.summary: A 34-year-old man with HIV who had sex with men was referred to our hospital after experiencing bloody mucoid stools for 6 months. He had initially presented to a local clinic, where haemorrhoids were suspected and topical treatment was prescribed. However, because his symptoms persisted, he was referred for further investigation. Colonoscopy revealed a circumferential 50 mm volcano-like rectal ulcer with an irregular, thick heaped-up margin and a deep ulcer base (figure A), accompanied by a smaller shallow round ulcer.

papers.title: In-cell discovery and characterization of a non-canonical bacterial protein translocation-folding complex
papers.summary: In-cell cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) combined with proteomics, integrative structural modeling, and bioinformatics enables discovery and functional annotation of uncharacterized proteins. In the minimal bacterium Mycoplasma pneumoniae, this reveals a complex that links Sec-based protein translocation and extracellular folding, capable of supporting both co- and post-translational pathways.

papers.title: Single-cell visual proteomics of a minimal bacterium reveals structural coordination of gene expression machineries
papers.summary: Cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) resolves and quantifies an almost complete view of bacterial translation, revealing how gene expression machineries coordinate across the processes of transcription, translation, and membrane engagement directly within a minimal bacterium.

papers.title: Resident tissue macrophages transfer selenium transporter protein to protect pancreatic cancer from ferroptosis
papers.summary: Resident tissue macrophages establish a selenium-rich niche at the pancreatic tumor border and protect invading tumor cells from ferroptosis by transferring Selenop protein to EMThi cancer cells.

papers.title: A pericyte-to-myofibroblast transition links APOE4 to cerebrovascular degeneration
papers.summary: APOE4 causes a pericyte-to-myofibroblast transition that promotes cerebrovascular fibrosis and perivascular amyloid accumulation. TGF-β inhibition reverses this pathological remodeling and thus presents a therapeutic strategy to restore cerebrovascular homeostasis in these high-risk individuals.

papers.title: Shifts in embryonic oxygen levels cue heterochrony in limb initiation
papers.summary: Mammalian embryos see a substantial increase in available oxygen once the placenta forms. This increase in oxygen exposure serves as a trigger for initiating the development of the hindlimb, thus controlling developmental timing and, more broadly, linking the maternal environment to evolutionary changes in body plan.

papers.title: Microbial signaling coordinates group oviposition and predator defense in migratory locusts
papers.summary: This study reveals an egg-associated bacterial signaling mechanism that couples reproductive synchronization with offspring defense in the locust L. migratoria, expanding the functional landscape of insect-microbe-predator interactions and demonstrating how microbial signals can shape complex ecological behaviors.

papers.title: Direct cell-to-cell transmission of retrotransposons
papers.summary: Retrotransposons can infect neighboring cells using a mechanism that relies on a small fusogen-like protein rather than on the envelope protein that is typically required for infection.

papers.title: Projection-defined modules reveal mouse motor cortex architecture
papers.summary: The mouse motor cortex divides into 16 spatially organized modules based on distinct subcortical projections. This specificity covaries with cortical connectivity patterns and cell-type composition along two spatial axes, thereby defining the rules by which motor cortex modules integrate with granularity into brainwide and precisely wired neuronal networks to influence movement.

papers.title: CD4 T cells convert transient responses to KRAS inhibition to durable remissions in pancreatic cancer
papers.summary: An AI-designed IL-21 mimetic converts transient KRAS inhibitor responses into durable pancreatic cancer remissions through CD4 T cells, independent of CD8 T cells and tumor MHC class I expression.

papers.title: Switching of transcriptional control from interferon regulatory factor 2 to interferon regulatory factor 1 drives innate immune cell activation
papers.summary: Toll-like receptor signaling activates proinflammatory interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs) even in the absence of interferon by triggering a shift from IRF2 to IRF1 occupancy at ISG promoters and enhancers. Newly translated IRF1 promotes proteasomal degradation of the weaker transcriptional activator IRF2 by engaging the E3 ubiquitin ligase SPOP.

papers.title: A geothermal amoeba sets a new upper temperature limit for eukaryotes
papers.summary: The amoeba Incendiamoeba cascadensis demonstrates that eukaryotic life can withstand temperatures beyond what was thought possible and sheds light on molecular strategies for survival in extreme heat.

papers.title: Chloroplasts balance energy production and stress resilience via a cold-induced signaling pathway
papers.summary: Cold-stress signals are transmitted to chloroplasts and subsequently trigger cold responses through an RAF-like bi-kinase module where cytoplasmic RAF3 and plasma membrane RAF6 translocate to chloroplasts, where they inhibit photosynthetic activity but activate nuclear cold-responsive gene expression.

papers.title: mRNA-encoding CD19-targeting T cell engager for refractory immune thrombocytopenia
papers.summary: An mRNA-lipid nanoparticle-encoded CD19×CD3 T cell engager depletes B cells with attenuated cytokine release in preclinical models. In three patients with treatment-refractory immune thrombocytopenia, treatment with this T cell engager achieved sustained platelet recovery over 6 months, suggesting that mRNA-encoded T cell engagers represent a promising therapeutic approach for resetting autoreactive immunity in B cell-driven autoimmune disease.

papers.title: Oligodendrocytes in central nervous system health and disease
papers.summary: Oligodendrocytes, predominantly known for their role in myelination, play a broader role in regulating the central nervous system, including feeding axons and reshaping neural circuits, with their malfunction in diseases ranging from multiple sclerosis to Alzheimer’s. This review covers oligodendrocyte biology and their therapeutic relevance.

papers.title: Toward autonomous science with agentic artificial intelligence
papers.summary: Biomedical artificial intelligence is advancing from tools that answer human-posed questions to agents that ask their own. Guo et al. assess this transition, including scaling logic, autonomous-laboratory trajectory, and the risks of hallucination, bias, dual use, and cognitive deskilling. This perspective argues that progress depends on responsible human-AI collaboration.

papers.title: Phosphate backbone epitranscriptomics: Discovery of natural RNA phosphorothioates and their writer machinery
papers.summary: Phosphorothioates, stereospecific modifications of the RNA phosphate backbone in anaerobic archaea, expand the epitranscriptome beyond nucleobases and ribose sugars. Installed by Esti enzymes at conserved rRNA and tRNA hotspots, these environmentally responsive marks stabilize tRNAs and support growth at high temperatures.

papers.title: 3D chromatin remodeling during domestication defines novel targets for crop improvement
papers.summary: Population-level 3D genome atlas of 34 semi-wild and 267 cultivated allotetraploid cottons reveals domestication-selected chromatin conformations that enhance cotton fiber quality and unlock cryptic breeding targets.

papers.title: Gliomas phenocopy an inborn error of metabolism to drive neuronal activity and tumor growth
papers.summary: Glioma-derived guanidinoacetate depolarizes neighboring neurons through γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) A receptors, and depleting this metabolite reduces both neuronal activity and glioma growth.

papers.title: Single-cell-resolved genome atlas of prokaryoplankton inhabiting the ocean’s interior
papers.summary: GORG-Dark presents genomes of 9,698 individual bacterial and archaeal cells from the ocean’s sunless interior. The atlas resolves depth stratification to abyssal waters, uncovers particle-attached Pelagibacterales, maps chemolithoautotrophy and biosynthetic gene clusters, and identifies a rhodopsin clade specific to the dark ocean.

papers.title: Programmed ribosomal frameshifting triggers translational stress to promote viral replication
papers.summary: Viruses such as SARS-CoV-2 can use programmed ribosomal frameshifting to turn off host translation and promote viral replication, expanding the known uses of programmed ribosomal frameshifting by viruses.

papers.title: Norway spruce spatiotemporal programs of conifer reproductive development
papers.summary: Spatiotemporal transcriptomics across conifer reproductive and vegetative shoots reveals candidate developmental regulators and evolutionarily conserved tissue patterning genes in seed plants.

papers.title: Copper ion-induced MYH9 polymerization executes cuproptosis
papers.summary: Copper binding drives MYH9 polymerization, triggering cytoskeletal collapse and cuproptosis. HThPA releases intracellular copper through glutathione depletion, exposing a therapeutic vulnerability in drug-resistant tumors.

papers.title: Metax enables accurate cross-domain taxonomic profiling of metagenomes
papers.summary: Metax is a cross-domain metagenomic profiler that uses genome-wide coverage evidence to improve species-level microbial profiling and distinguish supported taxa from artifacts. Across diverse datasets, Metax enables robust taxonomic profiling, pathogen detection, contamination assessment, and discovery of disease-associated bacterial and viral signatures.

papers.title: Mitochondrial ATP promotes T cell differentiation through chromatin accessibility
papers.summary: Cell-mediated immunity requires cytotoxic CD8+ T cells that adopt and maintain an effector phenotype. Here, D-α-hydroxybutyrate (DAHB) is shown to act as a metabolic adjuvant, driving the conversion of proliferating CD8+ T cells into cytotoxic effector cells by linking mitochondrial ATP production to chromatin remodeling and gene expression.

papers.title: Glycocalyx-edited mesenchymal stem/stromal cell therapy in advanced osteoporosis
papers.summary: Mesenchymal stem/stromal cell (MSC)-based therapy holds promise for reversal of bone loss in osteoporosis. This phase 1 study establishes the safety and feasibility of intravenous administration of glycocalyx-engineered human MSCs and provides evidence that MSCs derived from the bone marrow of older individuals with osteoporosis retain clinically meaningful osteoregenerative capacity.

papers.title: Architecture of the serotonergic projectome in the mouse brain
papers.summary: Serotonin neurons innervate nearly the entire mammalian brain, yet how their projections are organized has remained unclear. Systematic whole-brain serotonergic axon collateralization mapping reveals five projectomic groups that preferentially target functionally related regions, with each projectomic group connecting to specific spatial transcriptomic and behavioral profiles.

papers.title: Caloric restriction modulates genome-wide somatic mutation in mice
papers.summary: Mutations accumulate in cells with age, while caloric restriction extends lifespan across diverse animals. Grońska-Pęski et al. study the effect of caloric restriction on mutations genome-wide in mice, finding reduced mutation burdens across several tissues and cell types, thereby establishing that diet can alter mutation accumulation genome-wide during aging.

papers.title: Structural basis of a SWI/SNF-associated transcription pre-initiation complex
papers.summary: Cryo-EM and genetic analyses reveal that the SWI/SNF chromatin remodeler is an integral component of the transcription pre-initiation complex. The structures demonstrate how SWI/SNF facilitates transcription initiation through stabilization of PIC organization and concerted remodeling of the +1 nucleosome.

papers.title: Identification of the tendon/ligament stem cell in mice and humans
papers.summary: The tendon/ligament stem cell is identified, and dysregulation of differentiation in this cell is shown as a mechanism contributing to lumbar spinal stenosis.

papers.title: Tabula Sapiens 2.0: A comprehensive transcriptomic atlas of human cell types
papers.summary: An expanded atlas of human cells maps the expression of nearly all human transcription factors across 701 cell-type/tissue combinations and uncovers the heterogeneous nature of senescence across tissues and cell types.

papers.title: Oxygen-responsive bacterial glycosphingolipid links symbiont fitness and immune development in neonatal host
papers.summary: How do maternal gut bacteria seed the rapidly developing neonatal gut? Heo et al. show that Bacteroides fragilis produces a distinct membrane lipid that enables this strict anaerobe to tolerate a microaerobic environment. This finding highlights divergent evolutionary strategies among related species, most of which rely on lipids conferring broader fitness.

papers.title: Ratiometric transcriptional activation by protein degradation
papers.summary: By tethering a protein of interest to anti-CRISPR, protein degradation is transformed into amplified and programmable transcriptional outputs via Cas-based transcription factors, with sensitivity to protein loss tuned by the anti-CRISPR-Cas ratio. These synthetic circuits can be multiplexed to enable high-throughput discovery of protein-degrading and -destabilizing molecules.

papers.title: De novo pan-rhodamine binders for fluorescence microscopy from mammalian cells to extremophiles
papers.summary: We developed an AI-based and principled computational strategy for de novo design of Rhobins, compact pan-rhodamine binders with high brightness, reversible binding, and extreme stability. It enables superior live-/fixed-cell, super-resolution, and single-molecule imaging with properties surpassing existing tags. It also supports extremophile imaging at 75°C, inaccessible with current tools.

papers.title: Cross-species single-cell atlas of the striatum defines cell-type and subregion disease vulnerabilities
papers.summary: Single-nucleus RNA sequencing and spatial validation across human and mouse striatum define principles of neuronal specialization across cell types, subregions, and species. These findings lay the foundation for understanding cell- and subregion-resolved contributions to brain function and disease, including addiction risk, antipsychotic responses, Huntington’s disease vulnerabilities, and pharmacologically relevant species differences.

papers.title: Live-cell transcriptomics with engineered virus-like particles
papers.summary: Najia, Le, Borrajo et al. establish “cellular self-reporting,” a technology to export molecular analytes from cells in virus-like particles. The authors demonstrate how mRNA export enables longitudinal transcriptome-wide profiling of living cells by sampling cell media. This platform transcends the destructive nature of conventional transcriptomic analysis methods and reveals gene expression dynamics in complex biological systems in situ.

papers.title: Endogenous opioid dynamics in the dorsal striatum sculpt neural activity to promote goal-directed action
papers.summary: Cell-type-specific, time-locked release of the opioid neuropeptide dynorphin in the dorsomedial striatum is both necessary and sufficient for goal-directed behavior. Inputs from the basolateral amygdala trigger dynorphin release that engages retrograde Gi-coupled presynaptic inhibition via the kappa opioid receptor, revealing a rapid neuropeptide mechanism for shaping behavior.

papers.title: Genome-scale perturb-seq in primary human CD4+ T cells maps context-specific regulators of T cell programs and human immune traits
papers.summary: A dynamic atlas of gene regulation was generated by perturbing every expressed gene across 22 million primary human CD4+ T cells under resting conditions and following re-stimulation. The resulting map reveals context-specific regulators of immune programs and links regulatory pathways to naturally occurring T cell states and autoimmune disease risk.

papers.title: Human nuclear ribomes reveal DNA-embedded ribonucleotides as epigenetic modulators of transcription-associated DNA supercoiling
papers.summary: Human nuclear ribomes reveal that DNA-embedded ribonucleotides accumulate at promoter-associated regulatory elements and scale with transcriptional activity. RNase H2 and Top1 process these ribonucleotides to modulate DNA supercoiling, uncovering a previously unrecognized epigenetic mechanism underlying transcription.

papers.title: Myo-inositol metabolism counteracts mycotoxin hijacking and confers broad resistance to fungal diseases in crops
papers.summary: Xia et al. reveal that the Fusarium mycotoxin DON hijacks host central metabolism through NAD+-dependent enzymes to promote disease and identify MIPS as a key safeguard that redirects myo-inositol metabolism to drive PI(4,5)P2-dependent vacuolar sequestration of DON, maintaining metabolic homeostasis and conferring broad Fusarium resistance in crops.

papers.title: A commensal-derived sugar protects against obesity by regulating immunometabolism
papers.summary: Tan et al. identify a human commensal bacterium, Clostridium immunis—and its bioactive phosphocholine-modified exopolysaccharide (EPS)—that reduces visceral adiposity and weight gain in mice. By decreasing IL-22 levels, this EPS increases metabolic activity specifically in visceral fat. Metagenomic analyses suggest that this bacterial pathway may be conserved in humans.

papers.title: Dietary pectin remodels commensal bacterial surfaces to promote IgA-mediated protection from intestinal inflammation
papers.summary: Tang et al. reveal that dietary pectin drives Bacteroides uniformis surface remodeling to enrich the surface glycosphingolipid HexCer. Neutrophils sense this signal via CLEC4E to promote IgA production, which helps this bacterium colonize the gut lining and protects against colitis, uncovering a diet-microbe pathway that promotes a mutually beneficial relationship.

papers.summary: (Cell Host & Microbe 34, 942–958.e1–e15; May 13, 2026)

papers.title: The rice circadian clock orchestrates the rhizosphere microbiome to synchronize nitrogen supply with plant demand
papers.summary: Enhancing nitrogen use efficiency (NUE) is pivotal for sustainable agriculture yet constrained by spatiotemporal N mismatches. Du et al. find that the rice circadian clock orchestrates rhizosphere microbes to synchronize N supply with demand. Clock component Nhd1 drives rhythmic root exudation to regulate microbial N turnover, enhancing grain yield and NUE.

papers.title: Microbial indole-3-acetamide alleviates polycystic ovary syndrome through HIF-2α-ceramide signaling
papers.summary: Chen et al. reveal that C. aerofaciens mitigates PCOS pathology through activation of the adipose HIF-2α-ceramide signaling pathway. C. aerofaciens activates this pathway through production of indole-3-acetamide (IAM). Construction of an engineered probiotic strain expressing IAM synthase to stably produce IAM shows therapeutic efficacy in a mouse PCOS model.

papers.title: Hippuric acid metabolism by Corynebacterium glucuronolyticum-like bacteria promotes calcium oxalate crystallization
papers.summary: Qi et al. identify Corynebacterium glucuronolyticum-like (C. glucuronolyticum-like) bacteria enriched in the urine of calcium oxalate (CaOx) stone patients and show that they promote CaOx crystallization through hippuric acid degradation and biofilm formation. Hippuric acid or cranberry prevents C. glucuronolyticum-like bacteria-driven crystallization, providing a microbiota-based preventive strategy.

papers.title: A microbial chromatin remodeler drives gastric cancer progression and immune evasion by reprogramming the host epigenome
papers.summary: Xie et al. reveal that Streptococcus anginosus promotes gastric immune evasion via extracellular vesicles that deliver a bacterial chromatin remodeler to host cells, co-opting TEAD1 to upregulate ZDHHC11 and stabilize PD-L1 through palmitoylation. Targeting this axis potentiates anti-PD-1 therapy, offering a potential strategy to improve immunotherapy in SA-positive gastric cancer.

papers.title: Bacteroides acidifaciens enriched by KRAS mutation promotes colorectal tumorigenesis
papers.summary: Jiao et al. identify Bacteroides acidifaciens as a bacterial pathogen that accumulates in CRC patients and mice harboring oncogenic mutant KRAS. B. acidifaciens selectively promotes the tumorigenesis of KRAS-mutant CRC via the SusF-ARHGEF2 axis, forming a positive feedforward signaling cascade. Targeting B. acidifaciens or SusF-ARHGEF2 crosstalk may suppress KRAS-mutant CRC progression.

papers.title: Dual sensing activates antiviral reverse transcriptase for membrane targeting
papers.summary: Xia et al. discovered that phage SSB/SSAP or NrdAB-mediated dGTP elevation activates DRT2 to synthesize a repetitive neo gene by rolling-circle reverse transcription. The resulting Neo protein depolarizes bacterial membranes and induces cell death, while the DRT2 ncRNA template can be reprogrammed for user-defined DNA synthesis.

papers.title: Mobile virus-derived siRNAs drive plant antiviral silencing through reiterated 3–4 cell immunization
papers.summary: The movement of virus-derived (v)siRNAs between plant cells has prompted the widespread yet unproven assumption that they help immunize as-yet-uninfected tissues. Albertini et al. now show that reiterated 3–4 cell immunization events mediated by mobile vsiRNAs drive the core of plant antiviral RNAi and may paradoxically benefit certain viruses.

papers.title: Targeting a site of vulnerability on circumsporozoite protein inhibits Plasmodium vivax malaria infection
papers.summary: Limited knowledge of protective B cell epitopes on the Plasmodium vivax circumsporozoite protein (PvCSP) remains a roadblock to vaccine development. Visweswaran et al. identify an inhibitory vaccine epitope on PvCSP that elicits antibodies capable of blocking sporozoite invasion of host hepatocytes. Definition of the structural basis for epitope recognition by a neutralizing antibody provides a roadmap for vaccine design.

papers.title: Germinal center interleukin-4 microniches drive tissue divergence of IgE memory B cell responses
papers.summary: IgE recall responses sustain allergic disease, but their anatomical regulation remains poorly understood. Villazala-Merino et al. identify Tfh cell-derived IL-4 microniches within germinal centers as an anatomical checkpoint that favors IgE recall responses in lymphoid organs while limiting their generation in the lung mucosa.

papers.title: Sensory neuronal mTORC1 kinase signaling establishes neuroimmune memory that initiates allergic immunity
papers.summary: How cumulative environmental allergen exposures are encoded by peripheral sensory neurons to shape immune responsiveness is unclear. Zhu et al. show that protease allergens induce an mTORC1-dependent, metabolically trained state in sensory neurons that amplifies later neuroimmune responses to allergens and enables cross-sensitization to antigenically distinct allergens.

papers.title: Cancers modulate processing and presentation of p53 neoantigens to evade T cell detection
papers.summary: Mutations in TP53 occur early in malignant transformation and are generally present in all descendant tumor cells. Haratani et al. find a dearth of actionable neoantigens displayed in the cancer immunopeptidome and define various mechanisms whereby tumor cells prevent effective processing and presentation of p53 neoantigens.

papers.summary: (Immunity 59, 1–21.e1–e7; March 10, 2026)

papers.title: Twenty-year persistence of SARS-CoV-1 immune imprinting shapes antibody responses to SARS-CoV-2 infection
papers.summary: Our understanding of long-term sarbecovirus immune imprinting remains limited. Zhang et al. reveal persistent imprinting in individuals sequentially infected with SARS-CoV-1 and SARS-CoV-2 over two decades, characterized by redirected antibody targeting from the variable receptor-binding motif to conserved receptor-binding domain (RBD) core regions after breakthrough infection. These findings define the durability and molecular basis of antibody imprinting and inform pan-sarbecovirus vaccine design.

papers.title: A pulmonary innate lymphoid cell-driven serotonergic neuroimmune axis orchestrates airway hyperreactivity and cough hypersensitivity
papers.summary: ILC2s engage in bidirectional neuroimmune crosstalk that shapes diverse physiological functions, yet whether ILC2-mediated serotonergic signaling affects asthma pathophysiology remains unexplored. Luo et al. show that ILC2-derived serotonin promotes type 2 immunity and activates vagal sensory neurons, contributing to airway hyperreactivity, lung inflammation, and cough hypersensitivity upon RSV infection. These findings reveal an ILC2-neuron crosstalk in asthma pathophysiology.

papers.title: A distinct effector B cell population drives autoantibody production in SARS-CoV-2 infection
papers.summary: Autoantibodies (autoAbs) are linked to mortality and Long COVID, yet their cellular origins remain unclear. Yuan et al. identify a distinct B cell population (DN2 cells) as a key source of autoAbs during SARS-CoV-2 infection. These cells mirror lupus DN2s and carry a strong autoimmune genetic signature, linking infection-triggered autoAbs to autoimmune predisposition and Long COVID.

papers.title: “The Hole”: Poetry Like a Gunshot Wound
papers.summary: Medicine trains clinicians in a particular silence. Through diagnosis, we medicalize the causes of suffering—contusion, laceration, hemorrhage—as though renaming anguish might contain it, keeping it from spilling out of charts and into our own lives. Operating room and ward become, ironically, fluent in the language of suppression. Yet the horrifically wounded body insists on poetry. It is precisely here, in the rupture between what medicine measures and what human beings experience, that the poem becomes not decoration but necessity. In “The Hole,” poetry does not resolve this rupture or even fix the wound, in this case a gunshot to the patient’s head, another in an epidemic of harm. Instead, it plumbs the unspeakable, not by translating it into medical terminology but exposing the violence of what resists translation. papers.title: Intra-Arterial Alteplase After Successful Thrombectomy for Acute Ischemic Stroke
papers.summary: To the Editor Dr Renú and colleagues reported that adjunctive intra-arterial alteplase after successful thrombectomy “may improve functional recovery” in large vessel occlusion stroke. The randomized clinical trial provides an important test of a plausible reperfusion strategy, but the report leaves a key issue unresolved—the clinical recovery finding rests on a primary outcome that was changed during the trial.

papers.title: Intra-Arterial Alteplase After Successful Thrombectomy for Acute Ischemic Stroke—Reply
papers.summary: In Reply As described in the original report, the primary outcome was amended at month 12 to improve clinical relevance and interpretability, considering emerging randomized evidence and the established use of the blinded mRS score assessment. The amendment was implemented on February 10, 2025, after enrollment of 283 patients, of whom 214 had completed or were eligible for 90-day follow-up. No interim analyses had been conducted, and no outcome data by treatment group were available at the time of the amendment; therefore, the change was not informed by accumulating trial results.

papers.title: Review of Prepregnancy Care and Counseling
papers.summary: To the Editor I appreciate the expanded women’s health learning opportunities provided by the JAMA Network journals under the editorial leadership of Linda Brubaker, MD, MS. The comprehensive Review of prepregnancy care and counseling by Dr Cooper and colleagues will be a valuable resource for clinicians caring for women of reproductive age. I am curious whether the authors recommend preconception screening for hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection. The US Preventive Services Task Force, Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, and American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists recommend screening for HCV infection. Curative antiviral treatment for HCV infection is available.

papers.title: Review of Prepregnancy Care and Counseling

papers.title: Human iPSC models of myocardial infarction: From injury to repair and therapeutic discovery
papers.summary: Johnson et al. review how human induced pluripotent stem cells can model key stages of myocardial infarction, focusing on cell types involved across acute injury, repair, and remodeling. They examine current model strengths and limitations and discuss emerging applications in therapeutic discovery, patient-specific modeling, and regenerative cardiac repair.

papers.title: Punicalin targets RSV glycoprotein and fusion protein at non-overlapping sites to prevent viral escape
papers.summary: Xiong et al. identify that punicalin broadly inhibits respiratory syncytial virus subtypes and clinical isolates by targeting the viral G and F proteins at sites outside known resistance hotspots. It retains potent activity against drug-resistant virus and, when delivered by nebulization, reduces pulmonary viral burden and inflammation in infected mice.

papers.title: Multipronged enhancement of CART cell activity against ROR1 neoantigen by inhibition of H3K27 methyltransferase EZH2
papers.summary: Wang et al. report that inhibition of EZH2 and, to lesser degree, other epigenetic modifiers promotes expression of ROR1 neoantigen on malignant cells. CART cells targeting ROR1 are able to detect the neoantigen at very low concentration and, in combination with EZH2 inhibition, highly effectively eliminate the ROR1-expressing cells.

papers.title: iPSC-derived retinal organoids: Biological insights and progress toward photoreceptor replacement therapy
papers.summary: Mandai et al. review iPSC-derived photoreceptor replacement therapy, contrasting cone precursor and retinal organoid transplantations. They highlight host-dependent cone integration, gene-edited organoids for enhanced integration, and synaptic rewiring in the adult primate retina, providing a framework to restore vision in patients with untreatable retinal degenerations.

papers.title: Functional O-specific polysaccharide-specific antibody responses in young children following Shigella infection in Bangladesh
papers.summary: Bernshtein et al. show that functional antibodies correlate with milder shigellosis at any age, yet only individuals over 5 years of age mount lasting responses to the surface O-specific polysaccharide that drives Shigella uptake by phagocytes and triggers IL-1β and IL-18 release.

papers.title: Genome-wide cell-free DNA methylation profiling via TAPS for moyamoya disease diagnosis and postoperative collateral formation prediction
papers.summary: Chen et al. apply multimodal cell-free DNA (cfDNA) profiling via TET-assisted pyridine borane sequencing to moyamoya disease. They identify cfDNA methylation signatures that distinguish moyamoya disease from atherosclerotic cerebrovascular disease and predict postoperative collateral formation, supporting minimally invasive diagnosis and preoperative assessment of moyamoya disease.

papers.title: Combining pro-resolving therapy with cyclosporine A restores immune homeostasis and reduces toxicity in autoimmune bone marrow failure
papers.summary: Grazda et al. show that defective inflammation resolution persists in autoimmune bone marrow failure, despite standard-of-care cyclosporine A therapy. Combining resolvin E1 with cyclosporine A restores immune homeostasis while reducing toxicity.

papers.title: A blood-based metabolic signature for earlier detection of lung cancer
papers.summary: Irajizad et al. report a blood-based metabolite panel for earlier detection of lung cancer. The metabolite panel complements clinical risk models for lung cancer incidence and mortality. The panel provides a means for identifying ever-smoker individuals at elevated 1-year risk of lung cancer who would benefit from lung cancer screening.

papers.title: Therapeutic oligonucleotides as genetic medicines: The current state and future perspective
papers.summary: Godinho et al. provide an overview of nucleic acid therapies, a new class of programmable drugs that enable disease-modifying treatments by acting at the gene transcript level. The authors summarize key advances in chemistry and delivery and offer a perspective on the advances expected in the near future.

papers.title: Targeting RPL4 improves the therapeutic efficacy of PD-L1 blockade in liver fibrosis
papers.summary: Zhang et al. identify a key profibrotic function of FBXL6 in hepatic stellate cells through activation of the RPL4-YY1-PD-L1-PI3K-AKT-mTOR axis. Targeting RPL4 in combination with PD-L1 blockade achieves near-complete resolution of liver fibrosis.

papers.title: Early diagnosis and molecular classification of gastric cancer peritoneal metastasis by deep learning-driven single-cell lipidomics
papers.summary: Pan et al. combine single-cell lipidomics and graph deep learning to identify occult peritoneal metastasis in gastric cancer. The label-free platform detects rare free cancer cells, supports molecular stratification, and delivers patient-level diagnostic results within 30 min.

papers.title: Characterization of circulating neoantigen-specific T cell responses and public T cell receptors shaping immune memory in Lynch syndrome carriers
papers.summary: Duzagac et al. show that circulating tissue-surveillance neoantigen-specific T cells are detectable in Lynch syndrome carriers, even before cancer onset. Their metabolic states differ by disease stage, separating cancer-free carriers from survivors. Public TCRs spanning blood and tumor tissue open a non-invasive window for immunoprevention in mismatch repair-deficient cancers.

papers.title: Class visualizations and activation atlases for computational pathology
papers.summary: Gustav et al. introduce a concept-level explainability framework that exposes the morphology encoded by a pathology foundation model. The approach reveals prototypical histopathological features and maps the organization and overlap of tissue and cancer concepts, demonstrating that internal model representations reflect both task complexity and pathologist ambiguity.

papers.title: Proteogenomic analysis of pediatric and AYA high-grade glioma reveals age-dependent biology, female-male differences, and kinase targets
papers.summary: Tignor et al. perform a comprehensive proteogenomic analysis of pediatric and AYA high-grade gliomas and identify age- and sex-dependent biology, candidate kinase targets, and proteins and immune signatures associated with poor survival outcomes.

papers.title: Single-cell and spatial multi-omics reveal a recurrent multicellular niche at the tumor-stroma interface in multidrug resistance
papers.summary: Shen et al. map the evolutionary trajectory of multi-drug resistance (MDR) across cancers, revealing a biophysical spatial nexus formed by specific fibroblasts, macrophages, and tumor cells. They demonstrate that dismantling this multicellular barrier-like niche with an FAP/TREM2 bispecific antibody safely restores therapeutic sensitivity, highlighting a targeted strategy to resensitize MDR.

papers.title: Allosteric modulation of YTHDFs by ellagic acid suppresses triple-negative breast cancer via non-canonical activation of the HIF-1α pathway
papers.summary: Zhou et al. identify ellagic acid (EA) as an allosteric inhibitor of YTHDF proteins that binds to a conserved site shared across YTHDF family members. By disrupting YTHDF2-mediated RNA decay, EA stabilizes PFKFB4 mRNA to prevent HIF-1α degradation and upregulates BNIP3 expression, thereby driving triple-negative breast cancer cell death.

papers.title: Single-cell tracking reveals tumor-reactive T cell plasticity during melanoma TIL therapy
papers.summary: Sandholzer et al. track tumor-reactive T cells across TIL therapy in metastatic melanoma using single-cell RNA and TCR sequencing. They show how ex vivo expansion reshapes CD8+ and CD4+ T cell states and links type 17 T cell co-transfer and regulatory T cell expansion to treatment resistance.

papers.title: First-line fecal microbiota transplantation for the management of immune checkpoint inhibitor-mediated diarrhea and colitis
papers.summary: Wang et al. report the efficacy of a preliminary cohort of patients who receive first-line fecal microbiota transplantation for the management of immune-mediated diarrhea and colitis with multi-omics characterization. Response is seen in 10 out of 13 patients, with an increase in alpha-diversity in a majority of patients who respond.

papers.title: Neutrophil elastase-mediated myoepithelial loss is a therapeutic vulnerability in ductal carcinoma in situ progression
papers.summary: Transition from ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) to invasive breast cancer remains a key step in disease progression that is poorly understood. Taifour et al. show that neutrophil elastase disrupts the myoepithelial barrier to promote invasive progression, identifying neutrophil elastase as a potential therapeutic target for high-risk DCIS.

papers.title: Bi-hourly plasma proteomics during the first 48 h of life in an African cohort reveals distinct periods and sex-dependent immune development
papers.summary: Bennike et al. profile plasma proteins and cytokines/chemokines in 679 healthy newborns through mass spectrometry and immunoassays to characterize immune adaptation during the 48 h immediately after birth at bi-hourly resolution. They reveal non-linear trajectories and sex-specific differences especially during day-of-life one, providing a molecular framework for early-life immune development.

papers.title: Targeted insertion of an optimized donor DNA is effective in a humanized mouse model of dominant retinitis pigmentosa
papers.summary: Esposito et al. develop a donor-optimized, mutation-agnostic AAV-HITI strategy for dominant rhodopsin-associated retinitis pigmentosa that simultaneously disrupts the mutant RHO P23H allele and restores rhodopsin expression through targeted integration at the human RHO locus, improving retinal structure, function, and vision in a semi-humanized mouse disease model, up to one year.

papers.title: L013 promotes NRF2 degradation in NRFA-subtype esophageal squamous cell carcinoma
papers.summary: Yu et al. identify L013 as an NRF2-targeting agent that reduces NRF2 via UPS-associated degradation and A51-mediated suppression. L013 inhibits tumor growth in preclinical models, revealing therapeutic potential for NRFA-subtype ESCC.

papers.title: Intoxication and other subjective effects of preanesthetic opioids in surgical patients: A randomized controlled trial
papers.summary: Karlsen et al. show that patients experience marked undesirable effects but minimal desirable effects after preoperative intravenous opioids.

papers.title: Uncovering combination therapies for immune-mediated inflammatory diseases through systems biology analysis on longitudinal patient data
papers.summary: Martínez-Mateu et al. develop a computational framework that uses longitudinal blood transcriptomes from patients with immune-mediated inflammatory diseases to prioritize combination therapies. They identify anti-TNF plus anti-IL-6R as complementary in rheumatoid arthritis, localize the effect to CD14+ monocytes, and validate the combination in mice, nominating candidates for clinical testing.

papers.title: A stem-like chromatin program in small-cell lung cancer is associated with poor outcomes after chemoimmunotherapy
papers.summary: Kumar et al. use ATAC-seq and transcriptomic analyses to define recurrent chromatin programs in small-cell lung cancer. A stem-like program is associated with metabolic adaptation, reduced immune signaling, and inferior outcomes after chemoimmunotherapy, supporting further development of chromatin-informed biomarkers and therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Dendritic cell centric nanoengineering couples antigen acquisition and STING activation for cancer immunotherapy
papers.summary: Xiang et al. develop a dendritic-cell-directed, dual pH-gated nanomedicine that couples CD47-SIRPα relief at the tumor-dendritic cell interface with intracellular STING activation after uptake. This strategy enhances antigen acquisition and T cell cross-priming, suppresses tumor growth and metastasis, and supports the translation of STING immunotherapy.

papers.title: Transforming large language models into medical specialists via knowledge injection
papers.summary: Kim et al. review knowledge-injection strategies transforming general-purpose large language models into medical specialists—internalizing medical knowledge, aligning behavior with clinical norms, and grounding outputs in real-time evidence—plus multimodal integration and agentic AI, charting a roadmap toward safe, trustworthy clinical AI.

papers.title: This week in charts: Novo’s rise and fall and AI biotechs’ big haul
papers.summary: The latest installment in BioPharma Dive’s data visualization series features a closer look at Novo's stock performance and the recent run of fundraising success for AI drug discovery startups.

papers.title: Novo pursues long-acting obesity drugs; Acadia slumps on Alzheimer’s data
papers.summary: Novo’s latest alliance involves injectables given every one to three months. Elsewhere, Nektar won a legal spat with Eli Lilly and the FDA issued two approvals.

papers.title: RNAi drug specialist ADARx raises $446M IPO
papers.summary: ADARx is the only maker of RNA-based drugs to go public since 2024 and the first RNAi biotech to price an IPO in the U.S. in more than a decade.

papers.title: Grail multicancer detection test wins FDA advisers’ backing
papers.summary: Panel members said the first-of-a-kind blood test should not be used to replace medical guideline-recommended cancer screenings, however.

papers.title: FDA nominee Overton parries vaccine questions at Senate hearing
papers.summary: Pressed by lawmakers on Thursday, Trump’s pick as the next FDA chief said she’d “follow the law” on key decisions and work to speed early drug research.

papers.title: Merck reveals study success, and possible safety worries, for eye drug hopeful
papers.summary: A medicine acquired in a $1.3 billion buyout came through in the first of two pivotal studies in diabetic macular edema, though language regarding the drug’s safety stirred debate among analysts.

papers.title: Lilly’s latest China drug deal; Immunovant’s setback in lupus
papers.summary: Lilly wagered up to $3.35 billion in its fourth China-focused alliance since January 2025. Elsewhere, analysts are now more confident about one of Vertex’s top prospects and an RNA drug succeeded against a rare form of ALS.

papers.title: Enveda, an AI drugmaker, banks $311M in venture funding
papers.summary: Enveda, which is using AI tools to mine plants and microbes for drug prospects, has three candidates in human testing for immune diseases and obesity.

papers.title: Roche, Ionis RNA drug scores in kidney disease study
papers.summary: The results position Roche to bring a new kind of medicine to market for IgA nephropathy, a disease that’s drawn considerable attention of late from drugmakers.

papers.title: 9 pharma leaders sound ‘alarm bells’ on biotech’s decline in Europe
papers.summary: Frustrated by a slump that’s seen Europe lose ground to the U.S. and China, several top drugmakers are calling for speedier clinical trials, intellectual property protections and “fiscal flexibility.”
With Lundbeck steering its R&D engine toward increasingly specialized neuroscience targets, the Danish drugmaker is plotting a U.S. HQ move to one of the country’s preeminent biopharma hotspots.

A legal feud unfolding in New York is putting a spotlight on the work of a business development veteran who is credited for pioneering one of biopharma’s hottest dealmaking mechanism: the China “NewCo” model.
Travere Therapeutics CEO Eric Dube, Ph.D., is stepping down after overseeing the launch of the rare kidney disease drug Filspari.
Ahead of its upcoming merger with Supernus, Indivior Pharmaceuticals has ended its long-running collaboration with Addex Therapeutics to develop positive allosteric modulators (PAMs).
Novo has struck a 1.17 billion euro ($1.3 billion) deal to combine Nanexa’s long-acting injectable drug delivery platform with its obesity and Type 2 diabetes drugs.

Roche’s Genentech is paying Earendil Labs $55 million upfront to discover and develop multiple bispecific antibodies. The deal, which focuses on oncology, includes milestones that could take the deal's value above $1.5 billion.
ADARx Pharmaceuticals has overshot its own IPO ambitions, as fellow RNA-focused biotech City Therapeutics also plans a public listing.

The Senate Committee on Health, Education, Labor and Pensions (HELP) today questioned Heidi Overton, M.D., Ph.D., Trump’s pick for FDA commissioner, in a hearing marked by tightrope-walking on issues like vaccines, abortions, flavored vapes and whether or not President Donald Trump is capable of being wrong.
The NIH’s National Library of Medicine has released the pilot version of a new tool designed to help scientists plumbing the library’s digital trove of scientific papers find related research faster.
Fosun Pharma subsidiary Henlius Biotech has signed a $440 million biobucks deal with California-based Amberstone Biosciences to work on T-cell engagers.

Acadia Pharmaceuticals’ phase 2 Alzheimer’s disease trial has missed its primary endpoint, but the company and analysts alike saw enough encouraging signals to support the continuation of a phase 3 program.

Despite a major trial setback earlier this year and increasing questions over its efficacy, medtech Grail has beaten the odds and seen a positive recommendation for its multi-cancer blood test Galleri from FDA advisors.
Roche has penned a backloaded $2 billion deal with hematology biotech Atavistik Bio to develop allosteric small molecules for cardiometabolic diseases.

Merck & Co.’s Brunello trial has hit its primary endpoint, shedding light on the effects of a trispecific diabetic macular edema (DME) drug candidate that the Big Pharma bought in a $3 billion takeover.
Senator Todd Young (R-IN), chairman of the National Security Commission on Emerging Biotechnology, told Fierce why he's concerned about the growth of China's biopharma industry.
Adagio Medical has initiated a strategic review of its business and will lay off more than half its full-time workers as the maker of cryoablation devices faces delisting on the Nasdaq exchange.

As two Big Pharma players in the autoimmune CAR-T space face unexpected safety setbacks, Kyverna Therapeutics is reporting long-term clinical data that showcase sustained efficacy alongside an unblemished safety profile for its potential first-in-class candidate, miv-cel.
Eli Lilly has committed $100 million in upfront and near-term payments to InnoCare Pharma to form a five-target drug discovery pact. The deal features up to $3.25 billion in milestones.
Enveda has raised a $311 million series E round, positioning the nature-derived drug discovery company to pursue its goal of becoming a household name over the next decade.
The Department of War has awarded Flagship Pioneering $47 million to develop medical countermeasure technologies against emerging threats.
Immunovant has stopped development of IMVT-1402 in cutaneous lupus erythematosus after failing a midphase test, closing off one path to market for the anti-FcRn antibody.
Boehringer Ingelheim has dived deeper into its collaboration with Variant Bio by expanding the collaboration to cover cardiovascular disease to the tune of $250 million.
GSK has been operating a strategy of “balancing the West and the East” since the Big Pharma’s eyes were opened to the potential of licensing drugs from China two years ago, according to an executive.
Roche has reported a phase 3 win for sefaxersen in kidney disease, teeing up talks with regulators about the path to approval for the Ionis-partnered, would-be blockbuster candidate.
Medtech startup Anaconda Biomed has hauled in $53 million to help finish off work on a pivotal trial for its endovascular project.

papers.title: CRISPR-associated enzymes are mislocalized to the cytoplasm in iPSC-derived neurons, resulting in KRAB(KOX1)-specific degradation
papers.summary: CRISPR-based genetic tools face unique challenges in iPSC-derived neurons, including expression stability. Here, Cajka et al. show that SV40 NLS-dependent constructs fail to localize to neuronal nuclei, driving cytoplasmic dCas9-KRAB(KOX1) degradation. Alternative NLSs rescue protein localization and expression, revealing mislocalization as a key factor in CRISPR inefficiencies in postmitotic cells.

papers.title: The drifting biochemical basis of an essential molecular interaction
papers.summary: Phylogenetic and experimental reconstruction of an essential molecular interaction across 460 million years reveals that historical substitutions constantly strengthened or weakened random parts of the interface, gradually reshaping the pattern and biochemical basis of affinity as well as the effects of possible mutations.

papers.title: Plasma proteins are integral to cross-tissue gene regulatory networks implicated in cardiometabolic disorders and coronary artery disease
papers.summary: Bankier et al. perform a parallel multi-omic integrative analysis across multiple tissues, using data from the STARNET study, to show that plasma proteins are integral to cross-tissue gene regulatory networks (GRNs). Proteomic signatures for different GRNs are shown to be associated with cardiometabolic outcomes and risk factors.

papers.title: Sampling protein language models for functional protein design
papers.summary: Darmawan et al. introduce multi-mutant sampling strategies for protein language models that exploit epistatic interactions, together with a holistic in silico evaluation framework scoring relevance, quality, and diversity. Benchmarked across diverse protein fitness landscapes, their designs outperform standard single-mutant approaches, and the work offers practical guidance for protein engineering.

papers.title: Evaluation of anti-tumor drugs by simulating physiological absorption and metabolism with a multi-organoid system
papers.summary: Xiao et al. establish a multi-organoid system that integrates intestinal absorption, liver metabolism, and tumor response. This system captures drug activation and inactivation processes overlooked by tumor-only cultures, thus providing a more physiologically relevant approach for predicting the therapeutic efficacy and toxicity of drugs.

papers.title: Let there be multifunctionality: Uncovering the dynamical zoo of the AC-DC genetic circuit
papers.summary: Small gene regulatory circuits can encode a surprising diversity of dynamical behaviors. A biophysical model of the AC-DC motif reveals over thirty distinct bifurcation structures and shows how molecular regulatory architecture and binding affinity orderings determine oscillations, hysteresis, and multifunctional responses to a single signal.

papers.title: Genome-wide chromatin recording resolves dynamic cell state changes
papers.summary: Takei et al. introduce LagTag, a chromatin-based recording strategy for mammalian cells. Past chromatin states are recorded by time-gated m6A writing and recovered alongside present states from the same cell population by antibody-guided tagmentation, establishing a foundation for temporally resolved chromatin profiling.

papers.title: High-throughput cell-free profiling of SARS-CoV-2 RBD variants enables rapid and quantitative in vitro affinity landscape mapping
papers.summary: The team developed a high-throughput platform to rapidly measure how hundreds of viral mutation combinations affect antibody binding, generating 31,740 quantitative affinity data points. The resulting landscapes reveal how mutation combinations drive immune escape and enable accurate computational prediction of antibody-binding strength from sequence alone.

papers.title: PROFET predicts continuous gene expression dynamics from scRNA-seq data to elucidate heterogeneity of cancer treatment responses
papers.summary: Cheng and Gu et al. introduce PROFET, a framework that reconstructs continuous single-cell trajectories from sparse scRNA-seq time series. By combining particle-based gradient flows with neural force matching, PROFET accurately captures nonlinear cell-state dynamics and reveals heterogeneous responses and candidate surface markers associated with breast cancer treatment resistance.

papers.title: Gene expression noise is reduced in communicating synthetic cell populations
papers.summary: A major goal in bottom-up synthetic biology is the construction of multicellular synthetic systems capable of coordinated and robust collective behaviours. However, robustness is often limited by noise and variability arising from increased molecular complexity. Whilst communication has been implemented in synthetic multi-cellular systems, the ability for communication to suppress cell free gene expression variability in populations of synthetic cells remain unexplored. To address this, we encapsulated the Lux and Las quorum sensing gene circuits in lipid vesicles under cell-free conditions to test the effect of communication on reducing cell-free gene expression variability across the population. Our results show that communication, limiting expression resources, and membrane surface effects can reduce gene expression variability. Resource limited Gillespie simulations for transcription and translation show that communication-mediated coupling reduces population-level expression noise

papers.title: Boolean Logic-responsive FRET Biosensors via Genetically Encoded Autonomous Compilation
papers.summary: Forster resonance energy transfer (FRET) is commonly used to monitor protein-protein interactions in situ. The high spatiotemporal resolution and facile implementation inside complex molecular environments have spearheaded FRET's widespread adoption in biosensing. Despite these advantages, current FRET biosensors are largely restricted to the detection of the presence/absence of individual inputs and are thus unable to sense several multiplexable inputs simultaneously within complex milieu of biological environments. In this work, we introduce a generalizable strategy to construct genetically encoded protein-based FRET biosensors capable of recognizing multiple inputs following Boolean logic-type (YES/OR/AND) operations. These topologically specified FRET sensors powerfully expand the input capacity in sensing protein-protein interactions while providing a user-programmable platform for monitoring heterogeneous biological activities both in vitro and in living cells.

papers.title: AI-Guided Multi-Objective Engineering of Glucoamylase Enables Acidification-Free Starch Saccharification
papers.summary: Glucoamylase is essential for industrial starch saccharification, but the limited thermostability and near-neutral pH tolerance of fungal glucoamylases necessitate cooling and acidification of liquefied starch. Here, we developed an artificial intelligence-guided strategy to simultaneously improve the thermostability, pH tolerance, and catalytic activity of glucoamylase from Penicillium oxalicum (PoGA). Two property-specific machine-learning models, CASPE-T and CASPE-A, identified substitutions associated with thermostability and pH tolerance, respectively. Experimental screening identified beneficial substitutions in 11 of 21 CASPE-T and 12 of 22 CASPE-A candidates. Folding-energy-guided recombination integrated the two traits while maintaining structural compatibility. The optimal variant, PoGA T513E/Q305N, exhibited 2.21-fold higher specific activity than the wild type, with half-life extended from 22.3 to 57.9 min at 60 degrees C and from 16.6 to 64.7 min at pH 8.0. papers.title: Constructing Virtual Viruses in A Spatial Minimal Cell
papers.summary: Viral development links gene expression and genome replication to particle formation within a cell. Here we construct virtual viruses in a JCVI-syn3A-based spatial minimal cell. For mycoplasma virus P1, molecular events connect expression and replication to coarse-grained packaging, followed by a spatial reconstruction of membrane opening and particle release. Individual finite-size particles coexist, move across the boundary and undergo partial crossings and returns before complete exit. In contrast, Acholeplasma phage MV-L1 (L1) expresses its genes and accumulates genomes as the host continues to grow and develops a constricted shape. The coexistence of viral activity and continued host growth is qualitatively consistent with the non-lytic biology of group 1 acholeplasmaviruses. These reconstructions extend the virtual cell to the viruses that develop within it, linking molecular activity, particle behavior and host growth.

papers.title: Genetically inducible coordinators of cytokine signaling pathways for interrogating T cell motility
papers.summary: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy is promising for treating hematologic malignancies, but extending this success to treat solid tumors is challenging. Improving T cell phenotype to address this need is desirable, and one such property is increasing T cell infiltration into tumors. A promising potential approach comprises rewiring cytokine signaling using engineered receptors to change how the T cell responds to environmental cues. However, we currently lack the tools and mechanistic understanding to iterate and improve upon such strategies. Notably, receptors that rewire signaling make it challenging to decouple paracrine effects from those conferred by the signaling inducer. To address this gap, we developed a genetically inducible toolkit of proteins termed Constitutive Activators of Motility-associated Pathways (CAMPs). papers.title: A Dynamically Regulated Designed IL-2 for Tumor-localized Signaling
papers.summary: Cytokines mediate cell-cell communication to coordinate immune responses and hold clinical promise as immunotherapies. While natural cytokines are exquisitely regulated by immune cells, engineered cytokines have not yet matched this sophisticated regulation, limiting clinical efficacy and safety. IL-2 is an important cytokine involved in antitumor response, but its production is disrupted in the immune-suppressive tumor microenvironment. Here we designed a regulated IL-2 module, OUTSMART designed IL-2 (dIL-2), that functions robustly in solid tumors and reduces systemic activity that could trigger toxicity: we computationally redesigned IL-2 to have a novel topology that increases stability, preserves native IL-2R{beta}{gamma} interfaces, ablates IL-2R binding, and delivers IL-2 signaling to CD8+ immune-effector cells.
